class.name: VisionOSXRInterface
class.brief_description: visionOS XR implementation for rendering in immersive mode, hand tracking, and controller tracking.
class.description: This is a visionOS XR implementation. It has four modules: - the CompositorServices module, to render with Godot in immersive mode - the hand tracking module, using Apple's ARKit - the spatial controller module, using Apple's ARKit and GCController - the scene understanding module, using Apple's ARKit, for plane detection, scene reconstruction, image (marker) tracking, and world anchors. Those modules can be enabled/disabled independently. The rendering module uses the CompositorServices framework to render an Immersive scene. It supports the full and mixed immersion modes. To use this module, you must set the [member EditorExportPlatformVisionOS.application/app_role] export setting to [code]Immersive[/code]. You can choose the immersion style using the [member EditorExportPlatformVisionOS.application/immersion_style] export setting. You must use the Metal rendering driver, and only the Mobile renderer is supported for now. You can initialize this interface in the [method Node._ready] method of any of your nodes as follows: [codeblock] func _ready() -> void: var interface = XRServer.find_interface("visionOS") if interface and interface.initialize(): var viewport : Viewport = get_viewport() viewport.use_xr = true viewport.vrs_mode = Viewport.VRS_XR viewport.use_hdr_2d = true [/codeblock] Do not initialize the XR interface in the [method Node._process] method, as this will initialize it at some unspecified point in the middle of the frame rendering, possibly causing incorrect visionOS API usage. Enable the hand tracking module with the [member ProjectSettings.xr/visionos/enable_hand_tracking] project setting. It will populate the [code]"/user/hand_tracker/left"[/code] and [code]"/user/hand_tracker/right"[/code] XRHandTrackers. The [code]"left_hand"[/code] and [code]"right_hand"[/code] reserved [XRControllerTracker]s are always registered. They are driven by spatial controllers, hand gestures, and the system pinch (spatial events). Enable the spatial controller module using the [member ProjectSettings.xr/visionos/enable_controller_tracking] project setting. Connected accessories then drive the [code]"left_hand"[/code] and [code]"right_hand"[/code] trackers. [b]Spatial events:[/b] while the system pinch (look and pinch) is active, it drives [code]trigger_click[/code] and the [code]default[/code] pose of the pinching hand's [code]"left_hand"[/code] or [code]"right_hand"[/code] tracker, overriding hand gestures and accessories for that hand. The gaze selection ray at the start of each pinch is published as the [code]default[/code] pose of the [code]"/user/eyes_ext"[/code] [XRControllerTracker]. [b]Hand gestures:[/b] ARKit does not report gestures directly, so pinch and grasp are derived from joint positions. The [code]/user/hand_tracker/left[/code] and [code]/user/hand_tracker/right[/code] [XRHandTracker]s always carry [code]pinch[/code], [code]pinch_click[/code], [code]grasp[/code], and [code]grasp_click[/code] inputs. Those gestures are also mirrored onto the [code]left_hand[/code] and [code]right_hand[/code] [XRControllerTracker]s as [code]trigger[/code]/[code]trigger_click[/code] and [code]grip[/code]/[code]grip_click[/code], so gameplay built on [XRController3D] works without a physical accessory. A hand that has a spatial controller attached is driven by that controller instead. [b]Passthrough:[/b] [member XRInterface.environment_blend_mode] is a portable view of [member immersion_style]. Full immersion reports [constant XRInterface.XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_OPAQUE], while mixed and progressive immersion report [constant XRInterface.XR_ENV_BLEND_MODE_ALPHA_BLEND]. Setting it changes the immersion style to match. Whenever passthrough is visible the root viewport is switched to a transparent background, because CompositorServices composites passthrough where alpha is [code]0[/code]. [b]Scene understanding:[/b] enable plane detection, scene reconstruction, or world anchors with the [code]xr/visionos/scene_understanding/*[/code] project settings. Detected geometry is exposed through [VisionOSPlaneTracker] and [VisionOSMeshTracker], and anchors through [VisionOSAnchorTracker] and the [VisionOSSpatialAnchorCapability] singleton. Plane detection and scene reconstruction require world-sensing authorization; ordinary local world anchors do not. Anchor requests can also enable anchor observation lazily after native initialization, without enabling scanning.

method.name: add_marker_reference_image
method.description: Registers [param image] (for example a rendered QR code) as a reference image ARKit should look for, with its printed width in meters. When found, a [VisionOSMarkerTracker] is added to the [XRServer] whose [member VisionOSMarkerTracker.marker_data] is [param name]. Requires the [code]xr/visionos/scene_understanding/enable_image_tracking[/code] project setting and world-sensing authorization. Images may be registered before or after initialization; each change rebuilds the image tracking provider and re-runs the ARKit session. Returns [code]false[/code] if the image is empty, the width is not positive, or [param name] is already registered.

method.name: clear_marker_reference_images
method.description: Removes every registered marker reference image and its trackers.

method.name: create_spatial_anchor
method.description: Creates an ARKit world anchor at [param transform] and returns its tracker. Set [param shared] to [code]true[/code] to share the anchor with nearby participants when [method is_anchor_sharing_available] returns [code]true[/code]. Requires the [code]xr/visionos/scene_understanding/enable_world_anchors[/code] project setting.

method.name: get_marker_reference_image_count
method.description: Returns the number of registered marker reference images.

method.name: get_spatial_anchor_capability
method.description: Returns the same capability available through [method Engine.get_singleton] as [code skip-lint]VisionOSSpatialAnchorCapability[/code]. This does not create another ARKit session or world tracking provider. Check its status before requesting or applying an anchor pose.

method.name: is_anchor_sharing_available
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if world anchors can currently be shared with nearby participants.

method.name: is_image_tracking_supported
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if ARKit image tracking is available on this device. It is not available in the simulator.

method.name: remove_spatial_anchor
method.description: Removes an anchor created with [method create_spatial_anchor] from ARKit and the [XRServer].
